defects.defect: Wave B's size leaves out work that its own second phase does, and with it the wave has no room. The sizing file puts the 07:00 job, its school lines and its first digests on F051 (2.75 hours) and says G015's 1.75 hours for Jordan's inbox leave the job out; wave A spends all 2.75 on Tony's job. Wave B's count holds only that 1.75 plus half an hour for her lookup checks, yet its phase also creates her 07:00 job, hand-starts a digest and checks that it reaches her alone before the schedule is switched on. Counted from the records that is about half an hour and two steps more, so wave B is about 25 hours and 51 steps, not 24.5 and 49: on the hour line and one step past the step line. It is also the wave named to take wave A's lookup (2.25 hours) if wave A runs over; by its own give-way text that arrival pushes weather by the hour and then photos and PDFs to wave D and pulls the flyer dates out of wave C. So the first slip in the two plans that hold tests T1, T2, T3, T4 and T8 moves three cards across three waves.
defects.fix: Count Jordan's 07:00 job and digest in wave B (about 0.5 hour, two steps). Then make wave D the home of weather by the hour (F083, 1.25 hours): it is already the piece named to give way, needs nothing from wave B, adds no risk, and wave D's day-out phase is its first user. Wave B is then about 23.75 hours and 49 steps, and wave D about 17.75 hours and 36 steps, which still leaves wave D room for everything B and C can send it (photos and PDFs 2.25, flyer dates 1, evening text 2: about 23 hours). If F083 must stay because Tony has seen it in B, state wave B as 25 hours and 51 steps and say that the weather phase opening wave D is the expected case.

defects.defect: The 'try it first' phase is counted at 1 hour and 3 steps, which is light for what the records need. T7 has to be sent from iMessage, so a throwaway agent that holds the scheduling tool must be generated, reached by Tony's handle, deployed, waited on until the reminder fires, and removed with a second deploy. T5 here is a throwaway plugin deployed and removed, plus one turn each for two tools that no eval-only copy holds yet (the scheduling tool and the file-write tools), which have to be granted for the turn. My count is about 1.75 hours and 5 steps, which puts wave C at about 25 hours and 50 steps: exactly on the line, before the notes fallback (2.5 hours) that a failed T6 adds.
defects.fix: Count the phase at about 1.75 hours and 5 steps and give wave C as about 25 hours and 50 steps. Say in wave C that the flyer dates (F010, 1 hour, already the piece named to give way) open wave D unless the plan is under its hours when reminders go live; wave D has the room.

defects.defect: The exit test needs the 21:00 text to arrive by itself on day one, but the card sends no text at all when nothing is on tomorrow, and the job runs only on the evenings Tony names (starting point Sunday to Thursday). As written the test fails on a Friday or Saturday, or on an evening before an empty day, with nothing wrong in the build. Wave D's exit test handles the same problem by having Tony place test events; wave C's does not.
defects.fix: Add to the exit test: day one is an evening on which the job runs, and Tony places one test event on the shared calendar for the next day beforehand. Add that event to wave C's tony_provides.

defects.defect: The exit test starts from 'a weekday on which Jordan's 07:00 text arrived by itself', but her text is silent on an empty morning. Wave A's exit test plants four mails so the text cannot be empty; wave B lists only one test mail to Jordan, for her lookup question, with no day given.
defects.fix: Say that Tony sends the test mail to Jordan the afternoon before the sitting and that it carries a date or a deadline, so her 07:00 text has at least that line and her lookup question has its answer.

defects.defect: The goal has three parts (the 07:00 text, the mail question, and a daily check that tells Tony alone when a Google sign-in stops working). The exit test proves the first two and does not touch the third: the sign-in check is tested only once, in its own phase, about two weeks earlier in the plan.
defects.fix: Add one clause to the exit test: the daily sign-in check ran that day and reported every stored sign-in as working, and the record of the alert from the sign-in broken on purpose is in the evidence folder.

defects.defect: T3 has two outcomes and only one is sized. G003's record says that if a job added twice under the same key is doubled, the jobs script keeps a name-keyed comparison. The scheduler phase records which outcome was seen but says nothing about that extra work, and wave A has about an hour of room.
defects.fix: Add to the scheduler phase: if the throwaway job is doubled, the comparison is written into the jobs script there (about an hour), and that hour is what sends the lookup to wave B.

defects.defect: A failed shared-folder search leaves CRT-13 (3.5 hours) with no stated fallback. The handbook phase says the few handbook facts then go into the typed family facts, but the emergency card, sitter sheet and form kit read a plan page and a page per child from the handbook, and its card names no other home for them. The answer is known two plans earlier, because the shared-folder part of T6 is first run in wave C, yet neither wave lists the decision.
defects.fix: Add one line to wave C's notes phase and to wave E's get-ready: if the shared-folder search failed, Tony decides then whether the kit's facts go into the family file or the kit waits. List that decision under tony_provides, as is done for the other failed tests.

defects.defect: Note 13 says waves D and E can swap at Tony's word because neither depends on the other. The cards do not, but the give-way chain does: waves B and C send their pieces to the front of wave D, which has about 8.5 hours of room for up to 6.5 hours of arrivals (weather 1.25, photos and PDFs 2.25, flyer dates 1, evening text 2). Wave E has 4.75 hours of room, so if it ran fourth it could not take them all (about 26.75 hours).
defects.fix: Add to note 13: if D and E swap, what gives way from waves B and C still goes to the plan that holds wave D's cards and waits one plan longer.

defects.defect: Each exit test names the piece that may give way (rain by the hour and the planted PDF in B, the real flyer in C, the conflict watch in D, the test dose in E, the voice memos in F, the group in G, the print in H). The definition says a moved piece is built in the next wave 'under the check written for it', which covers its go-live check, but no exit test says what happens to its clause, so a wave that shed a piece cannot pass its exit test as written and the wave that took it never proves it.
defects.fix: Add one sentence to note 11: a piece that gives way takes its exit-test clause with it; the clause is struck from the wave it leaves and added to the exit test of the wave that builds it.

defects.defect: Waves I and J are under the floor of one plan: about 10.25 hours and 22 steps, and 14.25 hours and 29 steps. Between them 16 card hours carry 8.5 hours of getting ready and exit gates. Both can be executed, and the definition says why it split them (one new kind of risk each), so this is a cost to show Tony, not a break.
defects.fix: No change is needed for executability. If Tony wants full plans, there are two small ways: merge I and J as note 4 already offers (about 20.25 hours and 42 steps, phone first, screen control last), or move voice memos (F003, 4 hours, no new kind of risk, and the source of the voice Talk mode may use) from wave F to the front of wave I, giving wave I about 14.25 hours and wave F about 15.25.
